LESSON: CUBES AND CUBE ROOTS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers 1.1 Integers Simple and combined operations on Integers By the end of th
Topic 1.2: Cubes and Cube Roots

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Cubes and Cube Roots. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How do we work out the cubes of numbers?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. work out cubes of numbers by multiplication in real-life situations
2. determine cubes of numbers from mathematical tables in different situations
3. determine cube roots of numbers by factor method in different situations

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Cubes and Cube Roots.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Cubes and Cube Roots using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Discuss the volume of a cube, determine both the cube and cube root, and relate the two,
2. Read the cube of numbers from mathematical tables and relate it to cube roots,
3. Communication and Collaboration: speaking and listening as the learner works with peers to use stacks of cubes to demonstrate the concept of cube and cube roots.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we work out the cubes of numbers?
2. How do we work out the cube roots of numbers?
3. Where do we apply cubes and cube roots in real- life situations?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Cubes and Cube Roots is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
